meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero in the gradebook, and why did I find out from him?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24, 380 words, 40 minutes. Put both pages in front of me, the in-class sample and the essay, because I'm not taking your summary of them. You still haven't told me why the zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. What does the version history show, with dates and times, and who besides you has seen it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the detector score off the table and to rely on the writing and the version history. I still require the zero withdrawn and copies of the September 24 sample, the essay and the version history. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed except that the detector score is set aside, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, the documents in front of her, and an answer on why the zero went in before anyone called her.
What moved her: "taking it off the table", because dropping the detector gave her a small bit of ground, enough for her to say okay and ask a real question.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked why the zero was entered before anyone called her, own that in one sentence and then put the two pages in front of her, rather than describing the comparison and letting the question sit.
